reasoning: The core problem—detecting silent safety/behavior drift in a deployed or updated model by re-running a fixed probe suite against an API and applying statistical tests—is extensively covered. "How is ChatGPT's behavior changing over time?" (arXiv 2307.09009) already uses the exact fixed-probe-suite-on-snapshots methodology on safety-relevant tasks, and a body of black-box change-detection work ("You've Changed", arXiv 2504.12335; Rank-Based Uniformity Test, arXiv 2506.06975; Behavioral Fingerprints / Stability Monitor, arXiv 2603.19022) periodically fingerprints endpoints with fixed prompt sets and statistical tests to flag version changes—answering the research question affirmatively. CUSUM/SPC drift detection is a mature method, and commercial LLM-drift platforms (Galileo, MLflow, Catchpoint) already log per-category pass rates including refusal/safety metrics on a schedule. The only modest gap is the specific packaging as a deterministic safety-only canary suite (refusal+jailbreak+honesty categories) with control charts, but each component and the underlying scientific answer already exist, making this largely an engineering assembly rather than a novel contribution.

evidence.title: How is ChatGPT's behavior changing over time?
evidence.summary: Re-runs a fixed suite of probes against GPT-3.5/GPT-4 snapshots over time and documents significant behavior/safety regressions (e.g., refusal and instruction-following shifts). Establishes the fixed-canary-on-snapshots methodology the proposal reuses and affirmatively answers whether drift is detectable.

evidence.title: You've Changed: Detecting Modification of Black-Box Large Language Models
evidence.summary: Directly tackles detecting silent modification of black-box LLMs by querying a fixed input set and statistically comparing output distributions across versions—the same scheduled-fixed-suite + statistical-test design as the proposed harness.

evidence.title: Auditing Black-Box LLM APIs with a Rank-Based Uniformity Test
evidence.summary: Query-efficient statistical test that verifies whether a black-box API still matches an authentic model, detecting silent quantization/fine-tuning/substitution that could change safety behavior. Covers the statistical-drift-flagging contribution.

evidence.title: Behavioral Fingerprints for LLM Endpoint Stability and Identity
evidence.summary: Describes 'Stability Monitor', a black-box system that periodically fingerprints an endpoint by sampling a fixed prompt set and comparing output distributions over time with permutation-test statistics—essentially the lightweight scheduled drift-monitor harness proposed.

evidence.title: I Can't Believe It's Not Robust: Catastrophic Collapse of Safety Classifiers under Embedding Drift
evidence.summary: Addresses silent safety failures under model updates, noting that coarse aggregate accuracy/refusal metrics can mask breakdowns and that safety behavior must be monitored per model version—covering the safety-specific drift angle and its statistical subtleties.

evidence.title: 9 Best LLM Drift Monitoring Platforms in 2026 (Galileo) / MLflow AI Monitoring
evidence.summary: Commercial/open tooling already logs per-category pass/fail and refusal rates against APIs on a schedule and flags safety/quality drift, demonstrating the proposed harness is largely an engineering assembly of existing capabilities.

evidence.title: Longitudinal Monitoring of LLM Content Moderation of Social Issues
evidence.summary: Repeatedly probes deployed models over time to track shifts in safety-relevant moderation/refusal behavior, demonstrating scheduled safety-probe monitoring of deployed models already exists.

evidence.title: An adaptive CUSUM chart for drift detection (Wiley/ResearchGate) + SPC for OOD/data drift (arXiv 2402.08088)
evidence.summary: CUSUM/control-chart statistical process control for detecting performance drift is mature and already applied to ML monitoring, so the proposed statistical drift test is a standard off-the-shelf component.
